text:
elaine: Heads-up — I opened PR #462 for the Dedicated Capacity docs. Main things: autoscale policy examples need clearer min/max semantics, SLA table seems to list 99.9% but code snippet and SLO spreadsheet say 99.95, and we have a missing note about eviction/isolation decorators. Can reviewers please skim?
jordan: on it. can you paste the exact lines that disagree? want to avoid churn.
elaine: sure — in the SLA table row 'Availability (single-pool)' it says `99.9%` but in the YAML snippet under 'service.slo.target' the value is `99.95`.
sam: I saw that too when testing the terraform quickstart — the sample tfvar uses `slo_target = "99.95"`. probably a copy/paste from the older doc.
kai: I can fix the table text. also want to update autoscale example to show a min capacity of 0.5 vGPU equivalent (we should use weight-based examples not absolute GPUs). propose adding this snippet:```hcl# autoscale policy example resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "example" {  min_capacity = "0.5-vgpu"  max_capacity = "8-vgpu"  scale_policy = "cpu_and_latency"}```Thoughts?
marco: prefer we show both the TF and the CLI example side-by-side. for TF folks the `min_capacity` naming confused a few engs during the spike.
elaine: good call. can we add a short note about how reserved pools interact with canary rollouts and fallbacks? that'll prevent questions from infra teams.
jordan: yes — sample wording: "When a canary is deployed and capacity is constrained, traffic is routed to compatible model variants in lower tiers; reserved pools are only used if tenant-affinity is set." want to run that by security.
sam: also there's a link in the 'Isolation and preemption' section pointing to the old k8s blog post — needs to be swapped to our new 'eviction behavior' doc.
docs-bot: Reminder: PR #462 is assigned to @elaine for fixes and needs at least 2 reviewers by EOD.
kai: I'll push a small patch: update SLA table to 99.95, add TF + CLI autoscale snippets, and a one-paragraph note about reserved pool + canary behavior. will include a short migration note: "If you migrate pools, existing weights are preserved unless reset."
marco: can you also add a tiny snippet showing how to annotate dedicated jobs for isolation? like `isolation: "tenant:high"` — people search for "isolation decorator" often.
kai: yup, will add an example block and a link to the runtime isolation doc.
jordan: after kai's patch, I can run a quick spell/consistency pass. can we also fix the table's footnote to reference the SLA matrix doc id 5.2?
elaine: ack — thanks all. if no blockers I want the PR merged today.
sam: one more: the SDK snippet in examples uses `client.dedicated.provision()` but our new SDK uses `client.capacity.allocate()` — need to update that call site.
kai: good catch — I'll replace and add a one-liner comment about deprecation: `// old: client.dedicated.provision()`
jordan: looks good to me after those changes. @elaine if you confirm I'll approve.
elaine: I reviewed kai's draft patch in the PR, small nit about punctuation fixed. approved from my side. :thumbsup:
docs-bot: PR #462 status: changes pushed by kai, reviewers: jordan (requested), elaine (approved).
marco: merging once CI green. can someone drop the CI link here?
sam: CI passed on my run locally but I can't trigger GH actions from slack. I'll post the workflow link when GH finishes.
docs-bot: CI update: actions/ci-docs — success ✅ (build 118).
elaine: merged. thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short changelog blurb for the release notes.
jordan: thanks!
marco: nice, saved us a future support ticket.
docs-bot: Thread archived.
